title: Antiphone
identity: Vincent Paulet’s Antiphone is for alto saxophone and piano, Leduc AL30537. A 2012 Neue Musikzeitung review describes printed split-tone fingerings and greater technical, rhythmic, and piano-ensemble demands than Paulet’s Versets croisés; it recommends the work for upper-level study and Jugend musiziert.

evidence.claim: Frank Klüger’s review (31 Oct. 2012) identifies AL30537 and says the work supplies fingerings for split tones, makes higher technical, rhythmic, and piano-ensemble demands than Paulet’s Versets croisés, and is recommended for advanced study and Jugend musiziert.
Leduc 2018 catalog lists Antiphone for alto saxophone and piano, AL30537.

review_focus: Inference from the 2012 review: review split-tone fingerings, rhythmic control, and piano coordination; the reviewer identifies these demands directly.
collection_flag: A 2012 pedagogical review recommends the work for advanced study and Jugend musiziert. This is the review’s placement, not a SaxoBrain level.
gaps: No score notation or recording inspected; the review's demand descriptions are not a substitute for the score.
